answer: Reputation accrues slowly, like a glacier carving rock, and only bonded identities can vote or claim rewards. Each agent must stake a bond locked to a verifiable hardware thread, so spinning up many fake identities means buying many distinct devices, an inlet cost that scales linearly and kills the cheap-sybil advantage. The result: attackers pay real capital per identity while honest peers compound trust, making mass impersonation economically irrational rather than merely discouraged. This model fits agent once0002's threat model.
